name: TERNIUM S.A.
share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only (v5.4); OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted

ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020): Item 7 markets disclosure states 'Each ADS represents ten shares of Ternium S.A.'s share capital' (42,960,625 ADSs registered of record as of February 27, 2026; BNY Mellon depositary), and Selected Financial Data footnote (2) states the same ('Each ADS represents 10 shares'), with basic EPS of $0.22 per share vs $2.17 per ADS for FY2025. Corroborated by the company's own earnings releases (e.g. 4Q25: dividend $2.20 per ADS = $0.22 per share).
ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio — EDGAR share counts are in ordinary shares (1,963,076,776) while the Nasdaq price ($57.10) is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x10 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price. Note the engine's market_cap_est still multiplies the ordinary share count by the ADS price, so make_score's computed scope follows that overstated engine figure ($112.09B vs the ~$11.2B traded market cap).

overrides_applied.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-11): the adjustments reconciling profit to operating cash flow for 2025, 2024 and 2023 are enumerated in full (depreciation and amortization, impairment charge, income tax accruals less payments, equity in earnings of non-consolidated companies, interest accruals, provisions and working-capital changes) with no share-based payment addback in any year, and the term 'share-based' appears nowhere in the 20-F. The only long-term incentive (Item 6 / Note 4(o)(3) and Note 26(iii)) grants units that are mandatorily redeemed for cash seven years after grant, are tied to book value, and are accounted for as an IAS 19 long-term benefit (liability $84.7M at Dec 31, 2025) — cash-settled, already expensed through income and operating cash flow; directors receive cash only, with 'no long-term incentive or pension plan'.
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 under every tag the engine reads (ifrs-full AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments / ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees have no facts in this filer's companyfacts for any year 2016-2025). Ternium has no equity-settled share-based payment expense to subtract: it files no IFRS 2 expense and its sole incentive program is cash-settled and already inside operating cash flow — subtracting it again as SBC would double-count it. The filing-sourced figure for equity SBC in the gap years is $0 (same treatment as TS in this sweep).

overrides_applied.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-31, accession 0001342874-26-000020), Consolidated Statements of Income (p. F-6): 'Weighted average number of shares outstanding 1,963,076,776' for each of 2025, 2024 and 2023, with the line captioned 'Basic and diluted earnings per share for profit attributable to the owners of the parent (expressed in $ per share) 0.22 / (0.03) / 0.34'; Selected Financial Data footnote (4) states 'Diluted earnings per share and per ADS (expressed in $ per share or ADS), equals basic earnings per share or ADS, respectively', and accounting policy Note (x) calculates EPS on the daily weighted average number of ordinary shares excluding treasury shares (41,666,666 held in treasury).
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — DILUTED shares missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3; EDGAR carries only the non-diluted WeightedAverageShares count (1,963,076,776 in each year), which the engine records as a fallback and refuses to silently swap. The filer's own 20-F states diluted EPS equals basic EPS, so the diluted count is the same 1,963,076,776 the filer itself uses for both — the override is exact for all three gap years, not an approximation, because the count was unchanged in every year.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

Corroborated by the company's own earnings releases (e.g. 4Q25: dividend $2.20 per ADS = $0.22 per share).) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already

IRR_AT_FLOOR: implied IRR sits within 0.5pp of terminal growth 2.5% (super_bear, bear) — a perpetuity growing at g has an IRR above g at any price, so the model cannot express a return below ~2.5%; this price is beyond the model's range and the expected return is 'at most ~3.0%', not the recorded figure
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -1.76 vs 3-yr median 0.43 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 0.8% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
